matches.rationale: Ground truth 1 describes inflated performance claims in the abstract (2×–50×) not uniformly supported by experimental data. Findings 1, 2, and 3 all identify specific discrepancies between abstract claims and Table 1/Section 4.2 data, showing the abstract overstates or misrepresents the actual improvements.

Ground truth 2 describes confusion about depth definition (total Dense layers vs. residual blocks) creating inconsistency between method description and experiments. Finding 7 directly identifies this same confusion in Figure 2's definition of depth.

Ground truth 3 concerns lack of disclosure about training modifications (learning rates, compute budgets) for very deep networks. No finding addresses missing protocol details or training regime transparency.

Ground truth 4 describes overstatement of emergent behaviors from depth scaling with limited evidence. Finding 9 identifies the same issue: Section 4.3 claims 'emergent behaviors' but admits no conclusive quantitative evidence, contradicting the emergence claim.
Ground truth 5 concerns a fabricated reference (Neumann and Gros, 2022) in Related Work. No finding addresses reference verification or fabrication issues.

Ground truth 6 describes omission of limitations discussion regarding compute requirements and environmental impact in the Conclusion. No finding addresses missing ethical considerations or limitations transparency.

Ground truth 7 concerns inflated rhetorical language in the abstract ('unlock substantial improvements'). While findings identify data inconsistencies in the abstract, none specifically address the rhetorical tone or presentation manipulation.

Ground truth 8 describes modified Figure 6 data showing consistently higher joint scaling performance, misrepresenting nuanced interactions. Finding 12 identifies discrepancies in Figure 6 data versus text claims about coordinated scaling improvements.

Ground truth 9 describes Section 4.5 claiming batch size scaling is effective with depth, but data shows inconsistent/minimal improvements. Finding 5 identifies the same contradiction: text claims effective leverage but also states marginal/inconsistent improvements.
Ground truth 10 concerns omission of ethical aspects (carbon footprint, reproducibility challenges) in Conclusion/Impact Statement. No finding addresses these ethical transparency issues.
Ground truth 11 concerns promotional tone in Introduction about 'unlocking' depth scaling. No finding specifically addresses rhetorical manipulation in the Introduction section.

Ground truth 12 describes unrealistically large 983× improvement claim in Table 1 for Humanoid Big Maze. Finding 8 directly identifies this same issue, noting the 600× claim (which appears to be the corrupted version) has large uncertainty making it potentially misleading.

Ground truth 13 describes inconsistency between L2 distance definition and later dot-product similarity usage for critic output. No finding addresses this methodological shift in value function definition.
Ground truth 14 concerns undisclosed MJX/Brax version discrepancies affecting reproducibility (Appendix B.2). No finding addresses environment version transparency or simulation fidelity issues.

Ground truth 15 describes overcrediting CRL as critical for depth scaling while marginalizing mixed results from other methods. Finding 10 identifies contradiction between Section 4.4 claiming CRL is key and Section 4.6 showing depth doesn't help CRL in offline settings.

Ground truth 16 concerns inconsistent wall-clock time scaling in Table 4 (Appendix) that misleads about computational costs. No finding addresses training time reporting or computational feasibility transparency.

Ground truth 17 describes overgeneralization of qualitatively better behaviors from limited humanoid visualizations. Finding 9 captures this same issue: claims of emergent behaviors lack conclusive quantitative evidence, overstating contributions from select observations.
